title: Minimize premerge footprint and introduce lazy lint loader
author: Elena Park
release_notes: Reduces premerge CI runtime and compute cost by introducing a lazy-loading lint runner and an opt-in lightweight presubmit profile. No production behavior changes.
description:
Motivation: Premerge runs (esp. large monorepo changes) have been contributing to long feedback cycles and CI cost. This PR reduces the premerge footprint by deferring heavy lint/toolchain initialization to on-demand (lazy) runners and introducing an opt-in 'light' presubmit profile for small changes. Goals: (1) trim average presubmit wall-time, (2) lower ephemeral runner usage and cache churn, (3) keep developer feedback fast for small changes while preserving full checks on gated merges.

What I changed: introduced a lightweight presubmit profile and a lazy lint loader for the GitHub Actions presubmit flow. The lazy loader defers loading language-specific lint containers until file-glob heuristics indicate a linting step is required. A small presubmit manifest (ci/presubmit-profiles/light.yaml) defines quick smoke checks (fmt, unit smoke, deps verification) and runs by default for PRs that touch <= 10 files. Full presubmit remains available and is automatically triggered for larger diffs or when labels/paths require it.

Key implementation details (high level): - New composite action: .github/actions/lazy-lint-loader (shell + node shim) which inspects changed files, warms a minimal toolcache, and conditionally invokes language-specific runners. - Presubmit profiles: ci/presubmit-profiles/{light,default}.yaml and helpers to evaluate the profile based on changed paths and labels. - Cache policy: reduced prefetch of toolchains; caches are now keyed by path-hash + profile to avoid cross-profile pollution. - Dependency hygiene: bumped a few GH Action action versions and updated the devcontainer/toolchain manifest; updated lockfiles for the composite action test harness.

Testing & Validation: - Local smoke harness: ran the new lightweight profile against 120 historical PR diffs (sampled across repo teams). Results: average presubmit time down 28% and median runtime down 43% for small diffs. - End-to-end: ran full CI on branch; all integration and longtests passed on the full profile. - Canary rollout: enabled the lightweight profile opt-in for a pilot org and monitored for two weeks. Observed a 32% reduction in ephemeral runner minutes for participating teams.

Rollout Plan: - Merge behind a feature flag; opt-in teams can enable via repo setting. - Gradual opt-in on per-team basis; full default switch scheduled next quarter after broader canary. - Telemetry: added new metrics (ci.presubmit.profile, ci.presubmit.skipped_checks, ci.lazy_loader.invocations) visible in the CI dashboard.

Checklist: - [x] Introduce lazy-lint-loader composite action - [x] Add presubmit profile manifest and evaluator - [x] Update GH workflow definitions with conditional paths - [x] Bump action deps and update lockfiles - [x] Add unit tests for evaluator and smoke harness - [x] Canary and verify metrics

Notes: This change intentionally keeps full-surface checks intact for large changes; the light profile only optimizes quick iteration for small changes. The lazy loader reduces toolchain startup but keeps deterministic behavior by explicitly falling back to full runners if heuristics are ambiguous. If you rely on CI caching semantics, please review the new cache keys in .github/workflows/presubmit.yaml and in the toolcache helper (scripts/toolcache-key.sh).

review_comments: Samir Gupta (2025-11-14): Nice approach. Can you explain the criteria for falling back to full runners? Concerned about edge cases where generated files touch many langs.
